answer: Each identity must carry its claim across a public bridge, one claim at a time, and pay the toll with an ivory token carved only from its own verified jobs of this epoch. The token is one-use and written on the bridge ledger, so a second claim with the same token is turned back at the gate. A raven flies the bridge at a random moment seeded by the last close's hash and checks the token against the claimant's jobs; a token that does not match makes the raven cry and the claim falls from the bridge. Ten voices need ten tokens and ten separate crossings, because no toll can be lent to a clone.
